newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Hariri wins vote on new cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Hariri wins vote on new cabinet.

text.p: Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri easily won a vote of confidence in his new cabinet on Wednesday, arguing that Lebanon's economic and financial situation had improved dramatically under his four-year leadership.
"It is not true that the government was building bridges and forgetting about people in the past four years," he told parliament.
Army troops were deploying in Beirut on Wednesday evening to prevent anti-government demonstrations during a general strike planned by labour unions and opposition groups on Thursday.
The new government, formed on November 7, is the third headed by Hariri, a 52-year-old billionaire spearheading reconstruction from Lebanon's 1975-90 civil war.
Critics during the three-day confidence debate accused him of having no policy to help the poor and sinking Lebanon into heavy debt.
Former prime minister Selim al-Hoss, former speaker Hussein al-Husseini and firebrand MP Najah Wakim voted against the government. So did the parliamentary bloc of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah.
Speaker Nabih Berri said the 121 members present in the 128-seat house voted 102 to 19 for the government.
Hariri told the house that gross domestic product doubled to $11 billion dollars in his four years of office and the central bank's foreign exchange reserves rose 10-fold.
Lebanese banks deposits skyrocketed to $18 billion in that period and 130,000 new jobs were created, he added.

The statement of aims which the new government presented when seeking endorsement from the house promised to give priority to social policies -- housing, medical care, social security and transport -- as well as agriculture, industry and tourism.
